A.explanation: This has $\text{A}^{2}$ instead of $\text{A}^{-2}$ because charge is in the denominator when $k$ is made the subject, so ampere must have a negative power.

B.explanation: Rearranging to $k = Fr^{2}/q_{1}q_{2}$ gives $\text{kg m}^{3}\text{ s}^{-4}\text{ A}^{-2}$ in base units.

C.explanation: This omits $\text{s}^{-4}$ and has $\text{A}^{2}$, ignoring that force contributes $\text{s}^{-2}$ and that $q_{1}q_{2}$ contributes $\text{s}^{2}\text{A}^{2}$ in the denominator.

D.explanation: This omits the time unit entirely, but both force and charge introduce seconds that do not fully cancel.

hints: Notice the equation $F = kq_{1}q_{2}/r^{2}$ and make $k$ the subject as $k = Fr^{2}/q_{1}q_{2}$ to see which units go on top and bottom.
Recall the SI base units in this question: force $F$ is $\text{kg m s}^{-2}$, distance squared $r^{2}$ is $\text{m}^{2}$, and each charge $q$ is current x time, $\text{A s}$.
Combine the powers: multiply the top units $\text{kg m s}^{-2}$ by $\text{m}^{2}$, then divide by $(\text{A s})^{2}$ and simplify the powers of $\text{m}$, $\text{s}$ and $\text{A}$.
walkthrough: Write the force law with $k$ as the subject: $k = Fr^{2}/q_{1}q_{2}$, so the units of $k$ are (units of $F$) x (units of $r^{2}$) divided by (units of charge)$^{2}$.
State each quantity in SI base units: $[F] = \text{kg m s}^{-2}$ from $F = ma$, $[r^{2}] = \text{m}^{2}$, and $[q] = \text{A s}$ since charge = current x time.
Substitute the units: $[k] = (\text{kg m s}^{-2})(\text{m}^{2})/(\text{A s})^{2}$.
Simplify numerator and denominator: numerator = $\text{kg m}^{3}\text{ s}^{-2}$ and denominator = $\text{A}^{2}\text{ s}^{2}$.

Divide by subtracting powers: $\text{m}^{3}$ remains, $\text{s}^{-2-2} = \text{s}^{-4}$, and $\text{A}$ moves to the denominator as $\text{A}^{-2}$, giving $\text{kg m}^{3}\text{ s}^{-4}\text{ A}^{-2}$.
